activity.title: Things have been a little quiet since we were heads down building but…excited to finally announce the launch of SparkChat on the iOS App Store! Social media has become more media and less social. When I open up Facebook and Instagram, I don’t see any of my friends on there anymore - it’s one third ads, one third content from strangers, and one third AI slop. My friends are no longer on social media - I either meet up with them IRL or catch up with them in group chats. SparkChat is the social group chat app that actually helps you actually hang out with your friends. My college group chat kept a monthly dinner going for a decade, and we still spend two weeks every month going back and forth on finding a time and a restaurant. SparkChat fixes that. It uses AI and our group's social memory to find the best time and place for us to meet, based on everyone's schedules, locations, and food preferences. Then it books the reservation and adds it to our calendars. After a decade of apps built to keep us on our phones, I hope SparkChat helps us touch grass and see our friends more. Very grateful for our early investors and supporters, especially Y Combinator and our group partners Garry Tan and Christopher Golda . Y’all are the best :) Plz try it out and send us any/all feedback! 👇

HBSA and the Claude Ambassadors had the pleasure of bringing Claude’s first hackathon of the semester. Our theme was “Loving Grace” an ode to Anthropic’s mission to drive ethical AI use. Our contestants spent just four hours using Claude code to build projects that encapsulated this goal and they definitely delivered. Shout out to all the winners and contestants for all their hard work. Special thanks to guest speakers and judges David Bloom , Derek Wang , Jennifer Wang , and Paul Borowick for making this event possible. Along with Gyan Bhambhani , Marcus Wong , Samantha Yang , and the rest of the Haas Business Student Association (HBSA) team for helping us host this event as well as University of California, Berkeley, Haas School of Business and Berkeley Haas Entrepreneurship for providing us the venue, turnout was wonderful. #claudeAI #anthropic #HBSA #Hackwithclaude

We just wrapped another Builder Club meeting with Alicia L. from the Safeguards team at Anthropic! Alicia shared her journey from Cal student to Anthropic contractor. She broke down what safety and policy work actually looks like day to day, including the technical concepts she picked up along the way. To give folks more depth into what safety work looks like at an AI company, we ran a hands-on data labeling exercise and dove into how Anthropic thinks about when policies get triggered based on prompts. There's a lot more nuance there than most people expect, and that part sparked some great discussion. Safety and policy is one of the most underrated areas in AI right now. Huge thanks to Alicia for making it so approachable and for being so open about her path. Got another awesome speaker coming in April. Stay tuned 👀 thanks to team Emma Shen Angelina Nguyen Samantha Yang as always #AI #Safety #Anthropic #UCBerkeley #ClaudeBuilderClub #BuilderCommunity

First Claude Builder Club meeting of the spring ✅ This past Wednesday, we brought together 150+ Berkeley students to showcase what Claude can do. The energy was incredible; people from different majors and backgrounds all experimented with AI tools, many for the first time. We ran a quick prompting exercise in which teams would make and present a creative project in under 15 minutes. We were blown away by folks who went from prompt to fully-fledged games and short films by the end of the session. Wild to see how fast you can go from concept to demo with Claude. We have more events planned throughout the semester: workshops, hackathons, and demo nights. If you're at Berkeley and want to build, follow @claudeatucberkeley on Instagram for updates on our upcoming meetings. Thanks to the UC Berkeley Sutardja Center for Entrepreneurship and Technology (SCET) for the space, and to the ambassador team for making this possible. Emma Shen , Angelina Nguyen , Samantha Yang , Mason Arditi #Claude #ClaudePartner #AI #ArtificialIntelligence #UCBerkeley

I’m dropping out of Berkeley. Before you judge me, let me explain. This past semester nearly broke me. I burned out not once, but twice. I was taking five classes and trying to do everything “the right way” attending every lecture, lab, and discussion. I studied every single day and night. After classes, I’d hunt for empty lecture halls or lounge seats just to keep studying until 9 or 10 pm. Weekends weren’t breaks, they were catch-up days. On top of that, I was juggling clubs, extracurriculars, ambassador roles, networking events, mixers, socials, and trying to build real connections. Even the fun stuff took time and energy. And somehow, I still tried to show up for my friends the people who’ve supported me through everything. This isn’t a flex. It’s just the reality of trying to do everything you care about at once. It’s hard. Now I’m on winter break. Yesterday, I was back home in Florida at an arcade with my hometown friends. We laughed, yapped, smiled, and acted like nothing had changed. And for the first time in a while, my body and mind felt… calm. I realized how much I missed that feeling and how important it is to savor it. So no, I’m not actually dropping out of Berkeley. But I am dropping the lie that grinding 24/7 makes you successful. If you don’t rest, your body will force you to. Burnout isn’t a badge of honor. It’s a warning sign. You don’t need to disappear to be impressive. Take breaks. Touch grass. Protect your mind. It’s survival. And honestly? It might be the reason you don’t give up entirely. Take care of yourself. You deserve it. 💛 Comment "BREAK" if you also need to take a break and a chill pill😤✊️ #mindset #studentlife #selfcare #WorkLifeBalance

I am officially retiring from ragebaiting Hi, my name is Katie. EX-Cluely, ABG CMO. I once brought in over 14 million hate posts in a single day, reached Times Square, and even got on the news. Then I did it two more times, one with a minor, and hooked up with someone in Hawaii. Except... none of that actually happened. I just twisted the words to piss more people off. A month ago, I thought ragebait meant attention, and attention meant economy. Then reality hit. I lost deals. I lost VC interest. Especially in a B2B to B2C market... When you're funny, people don't take you seriously. And when you sexualize yourself for attention, business partners don't just ignore it. It shapes your reputation. It changes how people evaluate you before you've even opened your mouth. The lesson I learned is simple: Attention isn't the asset. Trust is. Since retiring from ragebaiting, I've closed more deals than ever. The best founders know how to go viral, have fun, AND still make sure their business is what people remember. Hi, my name is Katie. A 1X exit founder building a UGC agency. Influencer on LinkedIn and Instagram. 'Follow' Katie Chen to join my road to a million. Until next time, Katie Out. #Retired #GrandmaChen #StillABaddieTho

I fired my BEST employee today I know it sounds stupid. My company might go down. But here's why: 🫴Meet Alfonso. He's 21. A college dropout from Indonesia. When we met, he was broke. Fast forward to today... He single-handedly generated over 250 million views for our company in the past week. He helped build a business doing $20k+ per month I've never met someone who learns and adapts this quickly. Especially someone who started with absolutely NOTHING. Then a few weeks ago, he asked to talk. He told me he wanted to build something of his own. On the side, he'd started a YouTube channel. It exploded. 3 million followers in ONE MONTH. (wtf?!) I couldn't believe it. As a founder, every instinct tells you to convince your best people to stay Offer more money. More equity. A bigger title. But I realized something: Keeping him would've been great for my business... ...and bad for his future. So I fired my best employee. Not because he wasn't valuable. Because he was. Too valuable to spend his life building someone else's dream. Today, we still talk every week We exchange ideas, critique each other's content, and push each other to build bigger things. The best managers don't just build companies. They build people. And sometimes the greatest compliment an employee can give you is becoming someone who no longer needs you. Everyone should have an Alfonso in their life. And if you're lucky enough to hire one... Don't measure success by how long you keep them. Measure success by how far they go after they leave. This is your reminder to work so DAM HARD your boss is forced to fire you to pursue their own dreams (lol), I share my business and content lessons on LI everyday, Im Katie Chen , 1x founder, and founder of the only UGC agency that targets conversions, not views drop a 'follow', and hit me up for a chat Until Next Time, Katie Out. #ByeAlfonsoPleaseRememberMeWhenYouBecomeFamous
